words.enDefinition: a device designed primarily for playing video games

examples.en: My flatmate brought the game console into the common room after dinner.
examples.zh: 晚饭后，室友把「游戏主机」搬到了公共休息室。

examples.en: The club kept its game console in a cabinet beside the television.
examples.zh: 社团把「游戏主机」放在电视旁的柜子里。

words.enDefinition: a handheld unit with buttons and directional controls for games

examples.en: I was more comfortable using a gamepad than a keyboard for this game.
examples.zh: 玩这个游戏，我用「游戏手柄」比用键盘更顺手。

examples.en: The instructions showed which gamepad buttons to use for the first puzzle.
examples.zh: 说明提示第一道谜题要用哪些「游戏手柄」按键。

words.enDefinition: the arrangement of buttons and their assigned functions on a controller

examples.en: I checked the controller layout before handing the controller to my roommate.
examples.zh: 让室友接着玩之前，我看了「手柄按键布局」。

examples.en: The controller layout diagram showed the pause button near the middle of the controller.
examples.zh: 「手柄按键布局」图上显示，暂停键靠近手柄中间。

words.enDefinition: a small movable control on a gamepad operated by the thumb

examples.en: The tutorial asked me to move the left thumbstick toward the marked space.
examples.zh: 教程提示把左侧「手柄摇杆」拨向标出的位置。

examples.en: My friend showed me how the thumbstick moved the cursor on the map.
examples.zh: 朋友给我演示了「手柄摇杆」怎么移动地图上的光标。

collocations: use a thumbstick to move the cursor

words.enDefinition: a set of controller buttons for moving in different directions

examples.en: I used the directional pad to move one tile to the left.
examples.zh: 我用「方向键区」往左移了一格。

examples.en: The menu was easier to navigate with the directional pad than the stick.
examples.zh: 在那个菜单里，用「方向键区」操作比用摇杆顺手。

words.enDefinition: a control button along the upper edge of a game controller

examples.en: The tutorial showed a shoulder button for switching between the two toolbars.
examples.zh: 教程显示可以用一个「手柄肩键」在两个工具栏间切换。

examples.en: I pressed the shoulder button while trying out the new controller layout.
examples.zh: 试用新的手柄布局时，我按了一下「手柄肩键」。

collocations: the shoulder button on a gamepad

words.enDefinition: an on-screen cue showing which button to press

examples.en: I waited until the button prompt appeared beside the puzzle piece.
examples.zh: 我等到拼图块旁出现「按键提示」才操作。

examples.en: The button prompt changed when I switched from the keyboard to a gamepad.
examples.zh: 我从键盘换到手柄后，「按键提示」变了。

words.enDefinition: to change which inputs perform particular actions in a game

examples.en: I wanted to remap the controls because that button was difficult to reach.
examples.zh: 那个键够起来不方便，我想「重新设置按键功能」。

examples.en: The menu let us remap the controls before starting the next round.
examples.zh: 下一轮开始前，我们可以在菜单里「重新设置按键功能」。

collocations: let a player remap the controls

words.enDefinition: how quickly the game view responds to camera control inputs

examples.en: I lowered the camera sensitivity so I could look around more gradually.
examples.zh: 我调低了「视角灵敏度」，这样转动视角时可以慢一点。

examples.en: My friend checked the camera sensitivity after borrowing my controller for the round.
examples.zh: 朋友这轮借用我的手柄后，查看了「视角灵敏度」。

words.enDefinition: controller movement that signals an event or action in a game

examples.en: The controller used vibration feedback when I lined up the two pieces.
examples.zh: 我把两块拼图对齐时，手柄给了「振动反馈」。

examples.en: I turned off vibration feedback so the controller would feel steadier in my hands.
examples.zh: 我关掉「振动反馈」，这样拿着手柄时感觉更稳。

words.enDefinition: to exchange the controllers two players are using

examples.en: We decided to swap controllers between rounds so I could try the smaller one.
examples.zh: 两轮之间，我们决定「互换手柄」，让我试一下小一点的。

examples.en: My roommate asked whether we could swap controllers before the next puzzle.
examples.zh: 室友问下一道谜题开始前能不能「互换手柄」。

words.enDefinition: an option designed for one person to play alone

examples.en: I tried single-player mode while everyone else was still on the way.
examples.zh: 其他人还在路上，我先试了「单人模式」。

examples.en: The game opens in single-player mode unless you select a group option.
examples.zh: 这个游戏默认打开「单人模式」，也可以选多人选项。

words.enDefinition: a game mode for people playing together on one device or a local network

examples.en: We chose local multiplayer because everyone could sit around the same television.
examples.zh: 大家都能围坐在同一台电视前，我们就选了「本地多人模式」。

examples.en: My friend checked whether local multiplayer supported three people on one device.
examples.zh: 朋友查了「本地多人模式」能不能让三个人共用一台设备。

words.enDefinition: play through a network with people using separate devices

examples.en: We switched to online multiplayer when two friends went home for the break.
examples.zh: 两个朋友放假回家后，我们换成了「在线多人模式」。

examples.en: The menu lists online multiplayer beside the single-player option on the screen.
examples.zh: 屏幕菜单上，「在线多人模式」列在单人模式旁边。

words.enDefinition: a game in which players work toward a shared goal

examples.en: Our group picked a co-op game that was easy for newcomers to learn.
examples.zh: 我们小组选了一个新手也容易学会的「合作游戏」。

examples.en: I enjoyed the co-op game because we talked through each puzzle together.
examples.zh: 我喜欢这个「合作游戏」，因为每道谜题我们都一起商量。

words.enDefinition: cooperative play by people sharing one device in the same room

examples.en: We had time for couch co-op before the common room closed.
examples.zh: 公共休息室关门前，我们还有时间玩会儿「同机合作」。

examples.en: I looked for couch co-op so my friend could use the spare controller.
examples.zh: 我找了找有没有「同机合作」，这样朋友就能用备用手柄。

words.enDefinition: using separate areas of one display for different players' views

examples.en: The split-screen view gave each of us room to see our own path.
examples.zh: 「分屏」画面让我们各自有空间看自己的路线。

examples.en: We tried a split-screen session after connecting the second controller to the console.
examples.zh: 给主机接上第二个手柄后，我们试着用「分屏」玩了一局。

words.enDefinition: a mode where players take turns using the same device

examples.en: We chose pass-and-play because there was only one tablet on the table.
examples.zh: 桌上只有一台平板，我们就用了「轮流共用设备的玩法」。

examples.en: Pass-and-play worked well for our group during the train ride home.
examples.zh: 回家坐火车时，我们几个用「轮流共用设备的玩法」玩得挺顺。

words.enDefinition: an option for trying a game's controls or challenges without a normal result

examples.en: I spent a few minutes in practice mode before the others joined.
examples.zh: 其他人加入前，我在「练习模式」里玩了几分钟。

examples.en: The practice mode let us repeat the same pattern until we remembered it.
examples.zh: 「练习模式」能反复练同一套动作，直到我们记住。

words.enDefinition: a play option without formal competitive ranking

examples.en: We picked casual mode because two of my flatmates were still learning.
examples.zh: 有两个室友还在学怎么玩，我们选了「休闲模式」。

examples.en: The host explained that casual mode didn't affect our regular competitive rankings.
examples.zh: 房主解释，在「休闲模式」里玩不影响我们平时的竞技排名。

words.enDefinition: a play option where results count toward an official game ranking

examples.en: My roommate asked whether the match would count in ranked mode that evening.
examples.zh: 室友问那晚的对局在「排位模式」里算不算成绩。

examples.en: I tried ranked mode after learning how the points were displayed.
examples.zh: 弄清积分怎么显示后，我试了「排位模式」。

words.enDefinition: an option for building or experimenting without a fixed objective

examples.en: Our group used sandbox mode to plan a little model town together.
examples.zh: 我们小组用「沙盒模式」一起布置一个小镇模型。

examples.en: My friend likes sandbox mode because she can design whatever she wants.
examples.zh: 朋友喜欢「沙盒模式」，因为想设计什么都可以。

words.enDefinition: a way of playing organised around a game narrative

examples.en: I saved story mode for the weekend when I had more time.
examples.zh: 我把「剧情模式」留到周末时间多一点的时候再玩。

examples.en: The next chapter in story mode opened after we solved the puzzle.
examples.zh: 我们解开谜题后，「剧情模式」的下一章就开放了。

words.enDefinition: a game made for a group at a social gathering

examples.en: We picked a short party game for the break between revision sessions.
examples.zh: 复习间隙，我们选了一个玩起来很快的「聚会游戏」。

examples.en: The party game only took a minute to explain to everyone.
examples.zh: 这个「聚会游戏」只花了一分钟就给大家讲明白了。

collocations: a party game for a large group

words.enDefinition: a game mainly about solving problems or finding patterns

examples.en: I lent my friend a puzzle game that involved arranging coloured shapes.
examples.zh: 我借给朋友一个要排列彩色形状的「解谜游戏」。

examples.en: Our puzzle game lasted longer than expected because everyone suggested different solutions.
examples.zh: 大家各有解法，我们这一局「解谜游戏」比预想的要久。

words.enDefinition: a game that asks players to perform actions in time with music

examples.en: We played a rhythm game by tapping along to a gentle song.
examples.zh: 我们跟着一首轻柔的歌打拍子，玩了会儿「音游」。

examples.en: My roommate tried the rhythm game with the volume turned down.
examples.zh: 室友把音量调低，试了一下那个「音游」。

words.enDefinition: a game built around moving and jumping between platforms or surfaces

examples.en: The platformer started with a short level about jumping between floating steps.
examples.zh: 这个「平台跳跃游戏」开头是个很短的关卡，要在悬浮台阶间跳跃。

examples.en: I showed my roommate the platformer I played during the study break.
examples.zh: 我给室友看了学习间隙玩的那个「平台跳跃游戏」。

words.enDefinition: a game that gives each player a separate turn to act

examples.en: We chose a turn-based game so nobody had to rush a decision.
examples.zh: 我们选了「回合制游戏」，这样没人需要匆忙做决定。

examples.en: Our turn-based game left us time to discuss each move before making it.
examples.zh: 这个「回合制游戏」让我们每一步之前都有时间商量。

words.enDefinition: an option making on-screen objects easier to distinguish with colour vision differences

examples.en: I tried colour-blind mode because the tiles used similar shades of green.
examples.zh: 几种方块用了很接近的绿色，我就试了「色觉辅助模式」。

examples.en: The game added shapes to the markers when I selected colour-blind mode.
examples.zh: 我选了「色觉辅助模式」后，游戏给标记加上了不同形状。

words.enDefinition: to limit animations or camera movement in a game's display

examples.en: The accessibility menu let me reduce motion while keeping the other settings.
examples.zh: 无障碍菜单让我可以「减少画面动效」，同时保留其他设置。

examples.en: I chose to reduce motion before continuing with the puzzle on the screen.
examples.zh: 我选择先「减少画面动效」，再接着解屏幕上的谜题。

words.enDefinition: the starting selection screen with the game's main options

examples.en: I went back to the main menu to choose a different puzzle.
examples.zh: 我回到「主菜单」，换了一道谜题。

examples.en: The main menu offered a short practice session and an online option.
examples.zh: 「主菜单」上既有短时间的练习模式，也有联网选项。

collocations: an option on the main menu

words.enDefinition: a screen of options shown while the game is paused

examples.en: I opened the pause menu when someone knocked at the door.
examples.zh: 有人敲门时，我打开了「暂停菜单」。

examples.en: The pause menu showed us how much of the level was left.
examples.zh: 「暂停菜单」让我们看到这关还剩多少要玩。

words.enDefinition: a choice controlling how challenging the game is

examples.en: I changed the difficulty setting before showing the game to my flatmate.
examples.zh: 给室友演示游戏之前，我调整了「难度设置」。

examples.en: The difficulty setting affected how much time we had for each puzzle.
examples.zh: 「难度设置」影响每道谜题留给我们的时间。

words.enDefinition: a feature giving clues to help players solve a challenge

examples.en: We used the hint system when the last part of the puzzle confused us.
examples.zh: 谜题的最后一部分没看明白，我们就用了「提示系统」。

examples.en: The hint system gave me a small clue without revealing the answer.
examples.zh: 「提示系统」给了我一点线索，没有直接揭晓答案。

words.enDefinition: an explanation or practice sequence presented inside the game

examples.en: I finished the in-game tutorial during the break before everyone else arrived.
examples.zh: 其他人到之前，我趁休息时间完成了「游戏内教程」。

examples.en: The in-game tutorial showed me how to choose and move a piece.
examples.zh: 「游戏内教程」给我演示了怎样选择并移动棋子。

words.enDefinition: to choose which stage of a game to play

examples.en: I asked my friend to select a level we could finish quickly.
examples.zh: 我请朋友「选一个我们能很快通关的关卡」。

examples.en: The menu let us select a level by its number or name.
examples.zh: 菜单让我们可以按编号或名称「选择关卡」。

collocations: select a level from the menu
ask players to select a level

words.enDefinition: to make a stage available by meeting a game's condition

examples.en: We found out how to unlock a level by finishing the earlier one.
examples.zh: 打完前一关后，我们弄明白了怎样「解锁下一关」。

examples.en: I needed one more puzzle piece to unlock a level that evening.
examples.zh: 那天晚上，我还差一块拼图才能「解锁一个关卡」。

collocations: unlock a level by collecting pieces

words.enDefinition: a point in a level from which play can be resumed

examples.en: The game took us back to the checkpoint near the blue bridge.
examples.zh: 游戏把我们带回了蓝桥附近的「关卡检查点」。

examples.en: I was glad we reached a checkpoint before we had to pause.
examples.zh: 不得不暂停之前，我们到了一个「关卡检查点」，这让我松了口气。

collocations: go back to the last checkpoint

words.enDefinition: one place in a list for storing a saved game

examples.en: I chose a new save slot so I wouldn't overwrite my friend's progress.
examples.zh: 我选了新的「存档槽位」，这样就不会覆盖朋友的游戏进度。

examples.en: The game showed the date next to each save slot on screen.
examples.zh: 游戏在屏幕上每个「存档槽位」旁显示保存日期。

words.enDefinition: a menu option for opening an existing saved game

examples.en: I selected “Load game” and found the puzzle we started last weekend.
examples.zh: 我选择「读取存档」，找到了上周末开始解的谜题。

examples.en: My roommate pressed “Load game” to continue from our previous session.
examples.zh: 室友点了「读取存档」，接着上一次的进度玩。

words.enDefinition: to store your current progress before closing or leaving a game

examples.en: We chose to save and quit when the library started to close.
examples.zh: 图书馆开始清场时，我们选择了「保存后退出」。

examples.en: The game asked whether to save and quit before returning to the menu.
examples.zh: 回到菜单前，游戏询问是否「保存后退出」。

words.enDefinition: a menu option to continue playing after a pause

examples.en: I chose “Resume game” after helping my roommate find a spare controller.
examples.zh: 帮室友找到备用手柄后，我选择了「继续游戏」。

examples.en: The “Resume game” button took me back to the middle of the level.
examples.zh: 「继续游戏」按钮把我带回了关卡中途。

words.enDefinition: a display summarising how players performed after a game or round

examples.en: The results screen showed how many shapes each pair had matched.
examples.zh: 「结果页面」显示各组分别配对了多少个图形。

examples.en: We waited for the results screen before deciding whether to play again.
examples.zh: 我们等「结果页面」显示后，再决定要不要再玩一局。

words.enDefinition: to begin the current stage again from its start

examples.en: I asked if we could restart the level after missing the first clue.
examples.zh: 漏掉第一条线索后，我问能不能「重新开始当前关卡」。

examples.en: My friend chose to restart the level to try the quicker route.
examples.zh: 朋友选择「重新开始当前关卡」，试试更快的路线。

collocations: restart the level from the menu

words.enDefinition: the screen or stage where each player picks a character

examples.en: We were still on the character selection screen when my friend found the other controller.
examples.zh: 朋友找到另一个手柄时，我们还在「角色选择界面」。

examples.en: The music on the character selection screen stopped when everyone confirmed their choice.
examples.zh: 每个人确认选择后，「角色选择界面」的音乐停了。

collocations: return to the character selection screen
wait on the character selection screen

words.enDefinition: setting the traits or appearance of a new playable character

examples.en: I spent most of the break on character creation with my roommate.
examples.zh: 我和室友把休息时间的大半都用来「创建角色」了。

examples.en: The game offered more hairstyles during character creation than I expected.
examples.zh: 「角色创建」时，游戏提供的发型比我预想的多。

collocations: customise a look during character creation

words.enDefinition: a virtual room where players gather before starting a game

examples.en: I joined the game lobby while everyone decided which mode to play.
examples.zh: 大家还在商量玩什么模式时，我进了「游戏等候大厅」。

examples.en: We returned to the game lobby after finishing the group puzzle.
examples.zh: 完成小组谜题后，我们回到了「游戏等候大厅」。

words.enDefinition: a game waiting room limited to invited or permitted players

examples.en: We made a private lobby so just our flatmates could play together.
examples.zh: 我们开了个「私人房间」，只有合住的几个室友一起玩。

examples.en: My friend left the private lobby open while I went to get tea.
examples.zh: 我去拿茶时，朋友让「私人房间」继续开着。

collocations: invite friends to a private lobby

words.enDefinition: a code used to enter a particular game waiting room

examples.en: My roommate read out the lobby code before the next round started.
examples.zh: 下一轮开始前，室友念出了「房间邀请码」。

examples.en: I checked the lobby code after accidentally choosing the wrong room.
examples.zh: 不小心选错房间后，我核对了「房间邀请码」。

words.enDefinition: the player who manages an online group and starts group activities

examples.en: The party leader asked whether we were all ready before choosing a mode.
examples.zh: 「游戏队伍队长」先问大家准备好没有，再选模式。

examples.en: My friend became party leader when we switched to her saved game.
examples.zh: 切换到朋友的存档后，由她当「游戏队伍队长」。

collocations: ask the party leader to start

words.enDefinition: a message asking someone to join a group of players

examples.en: I sent a party invite after my classmate finished her evening seminar.
examples.zh: 同学上完晚上的研讨课后，我发了条「游戏组队邀请」。

examples.en: A party invite appeared while I was practising the first puzzle alone.
examples.zh: 我一个人练第一道谜题时，跳出了一条「游戏组队邀请」。

words.enDefinition: to indicate in a lobby that you are ready to start

examples.en: We decided to ready up after checking that both controllers were working.
examples.zh: 确认两个手柄都能用后，我们决定「点准备」。

examples.en: The host asked everyone to ready up when they had chosen a character.
examples.zh: 房主请大家选好角色后「点准备」。

collocations: wait for everyone to ready up
be the last to ready up

words.enDefinition: automatic grouping of players for an online game

examples.en: The game used matchmaking to find a few more people for our group.
examples.zh: 游戏通过「对局匹配」给我们这组找了几个玩家。

examples.en: We turned off matchmaking and invited only people from our residence.
examples.zh: 我们关了「对局匹配」，只邀请宿舍楼里认识的人。

words.enDefinition: an option to join a standard game with little setup

examples.en: I chose a quick match while waiting for the rest of my group.
examples.zh: 等小组其他人时，我选了「快速匹配」。

examples.en: The game offered quick match for players who didn't want custom rules.
examples.zh: 游戏给不想自己设规则的玩家提供了「快速匹配」。

words.enDefinition: to wait together for the same online game to be found

examples.en: I wanted to queue with friends instead of joining the session alone.
examples.zh: 我想「和朋友一起排队匹配」，不想自己进对局。

examples.en: The game let me queue with friends even while they were setting up.
examples.zh: 朋友们还在做准备时，游戏就让我能「和他们一起排队匹配」。

collocations: queue with friends for a match

words.enDefinition: a message saying an online game has been found for the player

examples.en: I heard a sound when “Match found” appeared on the laptop.
examples.zh: 笔记本屏幕上出现「已匹配到对局」时，我听到了提示音。

examples.en: The “Match found” message appeared just as I put down my cup.
examples.zh: 我刚放下杯子，屏幕就弹出「已匹配到对局」。

words.enDefinition: an option to watch a game without controlling a player

examples.en: I switched to spectator mode when all the places were already taken.
examples.zh: 玩家名额都满了，我就切换到「观战模式」。

examples.en: My roommate used spectator mode to watch how we solved the final puzzle.
examples.zh: 室友用「观战模式」看我们是怎么解开最后一道谜题的。

words.enDefinition: playing together online from different kinds of gaming platforms

examples.en: Cross-play let me join my roommate even though she used a different console.
examples.zh: 室友用的是另一种主机，「跨平台联机」让我也能加入。

examples.en: I checked whether cross-play worked between my laptop and his console.
examples.zh: 我查了自己的笔记本电脑和他的主机之间能不能「跨平台联机」。

words.enDefinition: to enter an online match after it has already started

examples.en: I asked whether I could join in progress after my study group finished.
examples.zh: 学习小组活动结束后，我问能不能「中途加入对局」。

examples.en: The settings allowed friends to join in progress without restarting the round.
examples.zh: 设置允许朋友「中途加入对局」，不用把这一轮重开。

collocations: allow players to join in progress

words.enDefinition: to return to a match you previously left

examples.en: I tried to rejoin the match after I closed the game by mistake.
examples.zh: 不小心关掉游戏后，我试着「重新加入原对局」。

examples.en: The menu gave me a chance to rejoin the match after I reconnected.
examples.zh: 重新连上后，菜单给了我一次「重新加入原对局」的机会。

collocations: offer an option to rejoin the match

words.enDefinition: another game between players who have just played each other

examples.en: My flatmate suggested a rematch while we still had the room.
examples.zh: 我们还能用一会儿那间屋子，室友提议「再赛一局」。

examples.en: We agreed to a rematch with the same teams after a break.
examples.zh: 我们商量好休息一下，队伍不变，「再赛一局」。

words.enDefinition: a voice channel shared by a group playing together

examples.en: We used party voice chat to compare clues as we played.
examples.zh: 我们一边玩，一边通过「队伍语音聊天」对照线索。

examples.en: The music was louder than my friend's voice in party voice chat.
examples.zh: 音乐比「队伍语音聊天」里朋友的声音还响。

words.enDefinition: a friendly expression used to acknowledge a completed game

examples.en: “Good game,” my classmate said even though our team came second.
examples.zh: 我们队得了第二，但同学还是说了声「打得好」。

examples.en: I typed “Good game” after the other team matched the final tile.
examples.zh: 对方配好了最后一个方块后，我打字说「打得好」。

words.enDefinition: a game played around a table with physical components or spoken rules

examples.en: Our group chose a tabletop game because the common room had no television.
examples.zh: 公共休息室没有电视，我们小组就选了一个「桌面游戏」。

examples.en: I tried a tabletop game that needed only paper, pencils and conversation.
examples.zh: 我试了一个「桌面游戏」，只需要纸、铅笔和交谈。

words.enDefinition: a game played with pieces or markers on a board

examples.en: We borrowed a board game from the residence desk on Friday.
examples.zh: 周五我们去宿舍前台借了一款「棋盘类桌游」。

examples.en: The board game fit on the little table next to the window.
examples.zh: 这款「棋盘类桌游」放得下窗边的小桌子。

words.enDefinition: a café where customers can sit and play tabletop games

examples.en: We met at a board game café after our last seminar.
examples.zh: 最后一节研讨课结束后，我们在一家「桌游咖啡馆」见面。

examples.en: The board game café had a shelf for short games and another for longer ones.
examples.zh: 「桌游咖啡馆」有个架子放耗时短的游戏，另一个架子放耗时长的。

collocations: meet at a board game café

words.enDefinition: an event where someone shows newcomers how a game works

examples.en: The club ran a learn-to-play session before its regular games began.
examples.zh: 社团的常规游戏开始前，先办了一场「游戏入门教学活动」。

examples.en: I joined the learn-to-play session because I hadn't seen the components before.
examples.zh: 我以前没见过那些配件，所以参加了「游戏入门教学活动」。

words.enDefinition: a booklet explaining how to set up and play a game

examples.en: We checked the rulebook after both of us wanted to move first.
examples.zh: 我们两人都想先走，就查了查「游戏规则手册」。

examples.en: The rulebook had an example of a complete turn on the last page.
examples.zh: 「游戏规则手册」最后一页举了一个完整回合的例子。

words.enDefinition: a small card summarising rules or actions for easy checking

examples.en: I kept the reference card beside me throughout the first round.
examples.zh: 第一轮我一直把「规则速查卡」放在手边。

examples.en: The reference card showed four actions we could choose from each turn.
examples.zh: 「规则速查卡」列出了每回合可选的四种行动。

collocations: a reference card for each player

words.enDefinition: a picture showing where pieces go before play begins

examples.en: We used the setup diagram to put the starting pieces in place.
examples.zh: 我们按照「游戏摆放示意图」摆好了起始棋子。

examples.en: The setup diagram was clearer than the long paragraph in the booklet.
examples.zh: 「游戏摆放示意图」比小册子里那段长说明更清楚。

words.enDefinition: to arrange the board and its starting pieces before playing

examples.en: My roommate helped me set up the board before the others arrived.
examples.zh: 其他人来之前，室友帮我「摆好了棋盘」。

examples.en: We took two minutes to set up the board for the new game.
examples.zh: 我们花了两分钟给新游戏「摆好棋盘」。

collocations: help someone set up the board
set up the board before playing
be ready to set up the board

words.enDefinition: an object moved or placed to represent a player or action

examples.en: I chose the yellow game piece so my classmate could use blue.
examples.zh: 我选了黄色的「棋子」，这样同学就能用蓝色的。

examples.en: The game piece fell off the board when we moved the table.
examples.zh: 我们搬桌子时，「棋子」从棋盘上掉了下去。

collocations: place a game piece on the board

words.enDefinition: a small object used to mark a value or state during play

examples.en: I put a game token beside the card to mark my choice.
examples.zh: 我在牌旁边放了一个「游戏标记物」，记下自己的选择。

examples.en: The blue game token showed how many chances we had left.
examples.zh: 蓝色「游戏标记物」显示我们还剩几次机会。

words.enDefinition: an individual surface where a player organises their cards or pieces

examples.en: I put my extra pieces in the top corner of the player mat.
examples.zh: 我把多余的棋子放在「个人游戏垫」的上角。

examples.en: The player mat showed where to keep cards we had already used.
examples.zh: 「个人游戏垫」标出了用过的牌该放哪儿。

collocations: place a card on the player mat

words.enDefinition: a sheet used to write down points during or after play

examples.en: I added my total to the score sheet for the final round.
examples.zh: 我把自己的总分填在最后一轮的「计分表」上。

examples.en: My friend checked the score sheet before we packed up the game.
examples.zh: 收游戏之前，朋友核对了「计分表」。

words.enDefinition: a printed path where a marker shows a running score

examples.en: The score track ran around the edge of the board beside the cards.
examples.zh: 「计分轨」沿着棋盘边缘一圈，挨着那些牌。

examples.en: I moved my marker along the score track after finishing the set.
examples.zh: 集齐一套后，我把标记沿「计分轨」往前移了。

collocations: a score track on the board

words.enDefinition: points counted to determine the winner of a game

examples.en: We earned victory points by connecting the paths on our own boards.
examples.zh: 我们把各自棋盘上的路线连起来，拿到了「胜利点数」。

examples.en: The rules explained when to count victory points from saved cards.
examples.zh: 规则说明了什么时间计算保留下来的牌给的「胜利点数」。

words.enDefinition: a supply of tokens or materials available during the game

examples.en: I returned the extra green tokens to the shared resource pool.
examples.zh: 我把多出的绿色标记物放回共享的「游戏资源池」。

examples.en: The resource pool ran low near the end of our second round.
examples.zh: 第二轮快结束时，「游戏资源池」里的资源不多了。

collocations: return something to the resource pool

words.enDefinition: the player who acts first in a game or round

examples.en: We picked a starting player before looking at any of the cards.
examples.zh: 我们在看牌之前先选了个「先手玩家」。

examples.en: The starting player read out the first clue for the whole group.
examples.zh: 「先手玩家」把第一条线索念给了大家。

collocations: a marker for the starting player
the starting player for this round

words.enDefinition: the sequence in which players may act during a game

examples.en: I checked the turn order when my friend came back to the table.
examples.zh: 朋友回到桌边时，我核对了「回合顺序」。

examples.en: The card showed the turn order on its bottom edge in small print.
examples.zh: 牌的下边用小字写着「回合顺序」。

words.enDefinition: to proceed around a circle in the direction of clock hands

examples.en: We agreed to go clockwise around the table after choosing the first player.
examples.zh: 选出先手玩家后，我们约好沿着桌子「按顺时针轮流」。

examples.en: The rulebook said to go clockwise from the person holding the marker.
examples.zh: 规则手册写着，从拿标记物的人开始「按顺时针轮流」。

words.enDefinition: a question asking which player should act now

examples.en: “Whose turn is it?” I asked after returning from the kitchen.
examples.zh: 我从厨房回来后问「轮到谁了？」

examples.en: My classmate looked around the table and said, “Whose turn is it?”
examples.zh: 同学环顾整桌，问「轮到谁了？」

words.enDefinition: to choose not to act on your current turn

examples.en: The rulebook said you could pass your turn without losing any points.
examples.zh: 规则手册说，可以「自己选择跳过回合」，不扣分。

examples.en: My friend asked whether you could pass your turn in the first round.
examples.zh: 朋友问第一轮能不能「自己选择跳过回合」。

collocations: be allowed to pass your turn

words.enDefinition: to lose the chance to act once because of a game rule

examples.en: The blue card said you would miss a turn if you drew it.
examples.zh: 蓝牌上写着，抽到后就会「按规则跳过一回合」。

examples.en: I asked whether a player would miss a turn after landing there.
examples.zh: 我问玩家落到那里之后会不会「按规则跳过一回合」。

collocations: make a player miss a turn
miss a turn in the next round

words.enDefinition: to play one more turn before the next person acts

examples.en: The card let me take an extra turn after finishing that set.
examples.zh: 集齐那套牌后，这张牌让我能「多行动一个回合」。

examples.en: My roommate asked why I could take an extra turn that round.
examples.zh: 室友问我为什么那轮能「多行动一个回合」。

collocations: be allowed to take an extra turn
choose to take an extra turn
let someone take an extra turn

words.enDefinition: an action permitted by the rules of a game

examples.en: I asked whether placing the tile sideways would be a legal move.
examples.zh: 我问把方块横着放算不算「规则允许的走法」。

examples.en: The rulebook gave an example of a legal move using two pieces.
examples.zh: 规则手册用两枚棋子举了个「规则允许的走法」的例子。

collocations: check whether it's a legal move

words.enDefinition: to undo a play you have already made

examples.en: We agreed beginners could take back a move in the practice round.
examples.zh: 我们约好，在练习轮里新手可以「撤回一步」。

examples.en: My friend asked if I wanted to take back a move after noticing the clue.
examples.zh: 看到线索后，朋友问我想不想「撤回一步」。

collocations: ask to take back a move
be allowed to take back a move
let someone take back a move

words.enDefinition: a rule for deciding the result when players have equal scores

examples.en: We checked the tie-break rule when two players finished on the same score.
examples.zh: 两名玩家最后分数一样，我们查了「平局判定规则」。

examples.en: The tie-break rule was printed under the example on the final page.
examples.zh: 「平局判定规则」印在末页例子的下面。

words.enDefinition: the approximate time a game takes to complete

examples.en: The estimated play time on the box was shorter than our lunch break.
examples.zh: 盒上写的「预计游戏时长」比我们的午休时间短。

examples.en: I checked the estimated play time before taking the game to the lounge.
examples.zh: 把游戏带去公共休息室之前，我查了「预计游戏时长」。

collocations: an estimated play time of an hour

words.enDefinition: the number of people a game or session can accommodate

examples.en: I checked the player count on the box before inviting another classmate.
examples.zh: 邀请另一位同学前，我查了盒子上标的「玩家人数」。

examples.en: The board changed shape depending on the player count for that round.
examples.zh: 棋盘会根据那轮的「玩家人数」改变形状。

words.enDefinition: a rule a group uses in place of or alongside the usual rules

examples.en: Our house rule allowed anyone to explain a clue twice.
examples.zh: 我们的「自定规则」允许任何人把一条线索讲两遍。

examples.en: I asked whether the timer was part of the rules or a house rule.
examples.zh: 我问用计时器是原规则里就有，还是一条「自定规则」。

words.enDefinition: the state or goal that must be reached to win

examples.en: We checked the win condition before planning our final few turns.
examples.zh: 安排最后几个回合之前，我们查了「获胜条件」。

examples.en: The win condition was to connect all four corners of the board.
examples.zh: 「获胜条件」是把棋盘四个角都连起来。

words.enDefinition: a person who presents a shared role-playing setting and guides play

examples.en: The game master described the town square before our characters arrived.
examples.zh: 我们的角色到达前，「桌面角色扮演主持人」介绍了城镇广场。

examples.en: Our game master asked everyone what kind of story they wanted to tell.
examples.zh: 「桌面角色扮演主持人」问大家想一起讲怎样的故事。

collocations: take turns being the game master

words.enDefinition: a set of cards used together for playing a game

examples.en: My roommate brought a deck of cards to the group picnic.
examples.zh: 室友带了「一副牌」来参加集体野餐。

examples.en: We checked the deck of cards after finding one under the table.
examples.zh: 在桌子底下找到一张牌后，我们核对了「一副牌」里的牌。

words.enDefinition: a single card from a deck used in card games

examples.en: I found a playing card in the corner of the game box.
examples.zh: 我在游戏盒角落找到了一张「扑克牌」。

examples.en: Each person chose a playing card to decide who would go first.
examples.zh: 每个人挑了「一张扑克牌」，来决定谁先出。

words.enDefinition: a playing card showing a jack, queen or king

examples.en: My friend asked whether a face card counted toward the bonus.
examples.zh: 朋友问「人头牌」能不能计入额外得分。

examples.en: The face card was the only one with a picture in my hand.
examples.zh: 我手上只有这张「人头牌」印着人物。

collocations: a hand with a face card

words.enDefinition: a card suit that outranks others under the rules of a game

examples.en: I wrote down the trump suit before we started the next hand.
examples.zh: 下一手牌开始前，我记下了「主花色」。

examples.en: The trump suit changed in the version we played after class.
examples.zh: 下课后我们玩的版本里，「主花色」是会变的。

collocations: the trump suit for this hand

words.enDefinition: a game where one player wins each group of cards played in turn

examples.en: We learned a trick-taking game from a friend in the common room.
examples.zh: 我们跟公共休息室的一位朋友学了一个「吃墩类纸牌游戏」。

examples.en: The club chose a short trick-taking game for the first half hour.
examples.zh: 社团选了个耗时短的「吃墩类纸牌游戏」，留给前半小时玩。

words.enDefinition: to play a card in the same suit as the first card

examples.en: The rulebook explained when players needed to follow suit during each trick.
examples.zh: 规则手册解释了每墩牌什么时候需要「跟出相同花色」。

examples.en: My roommate couldn't follow suit because she had no cards of that suit.
examples.zh: 室友手里没有那个花色的牌，所以不能「跟出相同花色」。

words.enDefinition: to play the first card in a trick

examples.en: I waited for my roommate to lead a card before choosing mine.
examples.zh: 我等室友「领出一墩牌的首张」，再从手里选一张跟出。

examples.en: The rules showed which player could lead a card after the break.
examples.zh: 规则说明了休息后哪位玩家可以「领出一墩牌的首张」。

collocations: ask who will lead a card
be the next to lead a card
lead a card of any suit

words.enDefinition: to take the set of cards just played in a trick-taking game

examples.en: My friend explained how to win a trick before we started playing.
examples.zh: 开始前，朋友讲了怎么「赢下一墩牌」。

examples.en: I thought I might win a trick with the card I had saved.
examples.zh: 我觉得自己留的那张牌也许能「赢下一墩牌」。

collocations: use a card to win a trick

words.enDefinition: the stack of cards players take new cards from

examples.en: We placed the draw pile within reach of both sides of the table.
examples.zh: 我们把「抽牌堆」放在桌子两边都够得着的地方。

examples.en: The draw pile had only two cards left when we stopped.
examples.zh: 我们停下来时，「抽牌堆」只剩两张牌。

collocations: take a card from the draw pile

words.enDefinition: the stack set aside for cards that have been discarded

examples.en: I kept the discard pile separate from the cards we could still draw.
examples.zh: 我把「弃牌堆」和还能抽的那些牌分开放。

examples.en: The top card of the discard pile showed a yellow circle.
examples.zh: 「弃牌堆」最上面的牌上画着一个黄色圆圈。

collocations: put a card on the discard pile
the top of the discard pile

words.enDefinition: to distribute cards to the people playing

examples.en: I offered to deal out the cards while my friends fetched chairs.
examples.zh: 朋友们去搬椅子时，我主动说来「给玩家发牌」。

examples.en: The instructions said to deal out the cards after counting the players.
examples.zh: 说明写着，数清玩家人数后再「给玩家发牌」。

collocations: offer to deal out the cards
ask someone to deal out the cards

words.enDefinition: to mix the order of the cards before playing

examples.en: We needed to shuffle the deck again before the next round began.
examples.zh: 下一轮开始前，我们得再「洗牌」。

examples.en: My classmate offered to shuffle the deck while everyone chose a seat.
examples.zh: 大家找座位时，同学主动说来「洗牌」。

collocations: ask someone to shuffle the deck

words.enDefinition: to divide a stack of cards and swap the positions of the sections

examples.en: My flatmate offered to cut the deck after I finished shuffling.
examples.zh: 我洗完牌后，室友主动说来「切牌」。

examples.en: We took turns being the person who could cut the deck.
examples.zh: 我们轮流当那个负责「切牌」的人。

collocations: ask someone to cut the deck

words.enDefinition: to take one card from the stack provided for drawing

examples.en: I had to draw a card before moving my piece that turn.
examples.zh: 轮到我时，我得先「抽一张牌」，再移动棋子。

examples.en: The rulebook said to draw a card after placing the last tile.
examples.zh: 规则手册说，放好最后一块方块后要「抽一张牌」。

collocations: draw a card from the pile
let a player draw a card
be asked to draw a card

words.enDefinition: to remove a card from your hand or play area

examples.en: I chose to discard a card to make room for another.
examples.zh: 我选择「弃掉一张牌」，腾出位置再拿一张。

examples.en: The game asked me to discard a card before ending my turn.
examples.zh: 回合结束前，游戏要求我「弃掉一张牌」。

collocations: discard a card at the end of a turn

words.enDefinition: the cards held by a player and available for use

examples.en: I checked my hand of cards before choosing which one to play.
examples.zh: 我先看了看自己的「一手牌」，然后才选出哪张。

examples.en: My friend set her hand of cards face down during the break.
examples.zh: 休息时，朋友把自己的「一手牌」牌面朝下放着。

collocations: look at your hand of cards

words.enDefinition: the cards a player receives at the beginning

examples.en: I looked at my starting hand before deciding how to begin.
examples.zh: 我先看了自己的「起手牌」，才决定怎么开局。

examples.en: The guide showed how many cards belonged in the starting hand.
examples.zh: 指南写着「起手牌」有几张。

words.enDefinition: the maximum number of cards a player may hold

examples.en: I reached the hand limit after drawing the two extra cards.
examples.zh: 抽完额外两张牌后，我达到了「手牌上限」。

examples.en: We checked the hand limit before ending the practice round together.
examples.zh: 练习轮结束前，我们一起核对了「手牌上限」。

words.enDefinition: to turn a card so its printed front is visible

examples.en: I had to turn a card face up before choosing my piece.
examples.zh: 我得先「把一张牌翻到正面」，再选自己的棋子。

examples.en: The host asked me to turn a card face up for everyone.
examples.zh: 主持人请我「把一张牌翻到正面」，给大家看。

collocations: ask someone to turn a card face up
turn a card face up on the table
choose to turn a card face up

words.enDefinition: to put a card into play so others cannot see its face

examples.en: I chose to play a card face down and reveal it later.
examples.zh: 我选择「背面朝上出一张牌」，之后再揭开。

examples.en: The rulebook said to play a card face down in the first round.
examples.zh: 规则手册写着，第一轮要「背面朝上出一张牌」。

collocations: choose to play a card face down
allow someone to play a card face down
play a card face down on the board

words.enDefinition: a protective cover that fits over an individual card

examples.en: My roommate slid the worn card into a clear card sleeve.
examples.zh: 室友把那张磨旧的牌放进一个透明「牌套」。

examples.en: I brought an extra card sleeve for the bent reference card.
examples.zh: 我多带了一个「牌套」，留给那张弯了的速查卡。

collocations: put a card in a card sleeve

words.enDefinition: to throw dice so they land on randomly selected faces

examples.en: The game asked us to roll the dice after choosing a colour.
examples.zh: 游戏要求我们选好颜色后「掷骰子」。

examples.en: I waited to roll the dice until my classmate had moved her counter.
examples.zh: 我等同学移好标记物才「掷骰子」。

collocations: take turns to roll the dice
roll the dice at the start of a turn
be the first to roll the dice

words.enDefinition: to roll the same die or dice again

examples.en: The rule allowed me to reroll if the dice landed off the mat.
examples.zh: 规则允许骰子掉到垫子外面时「重新掷骰子」。

examples.en: My friend decided to reroll after reading the optional rule on the card.
examples.zh: 朋友看了牌上的可选规则后，决定「重新掷骰子」。

words.enDefinition: a shallow container that keeps rolled dice from scattering

examples.en: I set the dice tray in the middle of the board.
examples.zh: 我把「掷骰盘」放到棋盘正中间。

examples.en: The felt dice tray made it quieter when we played after dinner.
examples.zh: 晚饭后我们玩的时候，毛毡「掷骰盘」让掷骰子的声音小了些。

collocations: place a dice tray on the table

words.enDefinition: a game where players answer questions about facts

examples.en: Our team chose a trivia game for the last twenty minutes.
examples.zh: 我们队选了个「知识问答游戏」，留到最后二十分钟玩。

examples.en: The trivia game had questions about food, music and local landmarks.
examples.zh: 这个「知识问答游戏」有关于食物、音乐和当地地标的问题。

words.enDefinition: a game where players use clues to work out hidden information

examples.en: We played a deduction game using pictures and a few simple clues.
examples.zh: 我们用图片和几条简单线索玩了个「推理游戏」。

examples.en: The deduction game was easy to explain once everyone saw an example.
examples.zh: 大家看过一个例子后，「推理游戏」很容易讲明白。

words.enDefinition: a game where players build their decks by adding cards during play

examples.en: My classmate introduced a deck-building game that started with very few cards.
examples.zh: 同学介绍了一款「牌组构筑游戏」，开局只有很少的牌。

examples.en: Our deck-building game ended before the common room had to close.
examples.zh: 公共休息室关门前，我们这一局「牌组构筑游戏」结束了。

words.enDefinition: a game where players add tiles to a shared or personal arrangement

examples.en: We chose a tile-laying game because people could learn by watching one turn.
examples.zh: 我们选了一款「板块放置游戏」，因为看一轮就能学会。

examples.en: The tile-laying game took up most of our small kitchen table.
examples.zh: 这个「板块放置游戏」占了我们厨房小桌的大半。

words.enDefinition: a game identity known to its player but concealed from others

examples.en: Each player had a hidden role that affected which clues they could give.
examples.zh: 每个玩家都有一个「隐藏身份」，影响自己能给哪些线索。

examples.en: I forgot my hidden role and checked the card under my hand.
examples.zh: 我忘了自己的「隐藏身份」，就看了看手下那张牌。

words.enDefinition: a mechanism where players gather matching or related items to earn points

examples.en: We learned how set collection worked by grouping the cards by symbol.
examples.zh: 我们按图案把牌分组，弄明白了「集套得分机制」怎么玩。

examples.en: The rules gave an example of set collection on the final page.
examples.zh: 规则最后一页举了个「集套得分机制」的例子。

collocations: a game based on set collection

words.enDefinition: a game where players describe characters' choices in a shared imagined setting

examples.en: I tried a tabletop role-playing game in which we planned a town festival.
examples.zh: 我试了一个「桌面角色扮演游戏」，我们在里面筹办小镇庆典。

examples.en: Our tabletop role-playing game started with everyone describing where their character lived.
examples.zh: 我们的「桌面角色扮演游戏」一开始，大家描述了各自角色住的地方。

words.expression: can I join the next round
words.lemma: can i join the next round
words.enDefinition: a question asking to start playing in the following round
acceptedEnVariants: can I join the next round

examples.en: “Can I join the next round?” I asked after seeing the board.
examples.zh: 看了看棋盘后，我问「下一轮我能加入吗？」

examples.en: My roommate arrived late and asked, “Can I join the next round?”
examples.zh: 室友来晚了，问「下一轮我能加入吗？」

collocations: ask “Can I join the next round?”
“Can I join the next round after dinner?”
“Do you think I can join the next round?”
